title: Term Premium Make-Up of the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
Every term's premium on the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) is booked as separate components.

| Component | Amount booked |
|---|---|
| Risk premium | the rated risk premium the Risk Rating 2.0 rating engine returned for the term |
| ICC premium | the rated ICC premium the engine returned for the term |
| Federal Policy Fee | the rated Federal Policy Fee the engine returned for the term (on an RCBAP the engine's figure already reflects the number of units) |
| Reserve Fund Assessment | the tier's Reserve Fund Assessment percentage of the sum of the risk premium and ICC premium, rounded to the cent |
| HFIAA surcharge | the tier's HFIAA surcharge, on every policy of this category, because none of them is a primary residence |
| Probation surcharge | booked only when the community is on probation, at the tier's probation surcharge per term |

**Rules.**
1. The desk never recalculates the risk premium, ICC premium or Federal Policy Fee; they are read from the rated figures on the policy.
2. The HFIAA surcharge, Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge are booked once per term at new business or renewal and never on an endorsement.
3. A component of zero is not booked, and the total term premium is the sum of the booked components.

## Worked term premium (hypothetical rated figures)

Rated risk premium 3,400.00, rated ICC premium 75.00, rated Federal Policy Fee 250.00, community not on probation, Reserve Fund Assessment percentage taken from the premium charges schedule as 18 percent:

- Reserve Fund Assessment: 18 percent of 3,475.00, which is 625.50.
- HFIAA surcharge: the schedule figure for the tier.
- Probation surcharge: not booked, because the community is not on probation (a zero component is not booked).
- Total term premium: 3,400.00 plus 75.00 plus 625.50 plus 250.00 plus the HFIAA surcharge.

If the same community were on probation, the probation surcharge would be booked as one more component of the term.
